g.title: of respondents said they ask people for directions when travelling somewhere unfamiliar.
Despite having access to digital navigation tools, asking people remains the most common way respondents navigate unfamiliar destinations.
of respondents identified uncertainty about transport fares as a challenge.
Knowing where to go isn't the only uncertainty. Commuters also need to know how much they'll be expected to pay.
of respondents identified unclear directions as a challenge.
A destination name alone doesn't tell someone what to do next. For public transport users, directions need to translate a route into clear, actionable steps.
of respondents were aware that Google Maps supports public transport navigation.

This showed me that the opportunity wasn't simply to introduce digital navigation. People already knew and used digital tools. The bigger opportunity was to explore how public transport navigation could be made clearer and easier to follow.
Existing navigation isn't always easy to use
Google Map’s public transport navigation received an average ease-of-use rating of approximately: 2.7 / 5
